heading: Book Pick: "The Psychology of Money"
body: Morgan Housel's core argument: financial success is less about what you know and more about how you behave under uncertainty. A short, highly readable entry point for anyone who finds finance intimidating but wants to actually understand their own money decisions.

heading: Book Pick: "Let's Talk Money" by Monika Halan
body: One of the clearest India-specific personal finance books available — covers insurance, investing basics, and real rupee examples instead of generic global advice. A strong first finance book for Indian readers specifically.

heading: Book Pick: "Rich Dad Poor Dad"
body: Robert Kiyosaki's framing of assets vs liabilities is simple but genuinely reframes how a lot of first-time readers think about spending decisions. Treat the specific investment advice with some skepticism — the mindset shift is the valuable part.

heading: Book Pick: "The Intelligent Investor"
body: Benjamin Graham's classic on value investing and margin of safety — dense in places, but the core ideas (buying below intrinsic value, staying emotionally detached from market swings) remain foundational to long-term investing nearly a century later.

heading: Book Pick: "Coffee Can Investing"
body: Saurabh Mukherjea's India-specific case for buying quality businesses and holding them for the very long term with minimal trading — a useful counterweight for readers tempted toward frequent trading or market timing.

heading: Book Pick: "I Will Teach You to Be Rich"
body: Ramit Sethi's practical, step-by-step approach to automating savings, negotiating bills, and building a 'conscious spending plan' — less theory, more a checklist you can actually implement in a weekend.

heading: Book Pick: "The Millionaire Next Door"
body: Research-driven look at how most actual US millionaires live well below their visible means rather than showing wealth outwardly. The underlying lesson — net worth over appearances — travels well beyond its US setting.

heading: Book Pick: "Thinking, Fast and Slow"
body: Not a finance book directly, but Daniel Kahneman's work on cognitive biases (loss aversion, anchoring, overconfidence) explains much of why investors make irrational decisions with money — essential background for understanding your own behavior.

heading: Book Pick: "One Up on Wall Street"
body: Peter Lynch's case for 'investing in what you know' — using everyday observations about businesses and products to spot opportunities before Wall Street analysts catch on. A good read once you're past the absolute basics.

heading: Book Pick: "Your Money or Your Life"
body: Reframes every purchase in terms of the hours of life-energy it cost to earn that money — a genuinely different lens on spending that many readers say permanently changed how they evaluate purchases.

heading: Book Pick: "The Barefoot Investor" (India-adapted lens)
body: Scott Pape's bucket-based approach to splitting income (daily expenses, splurge, smile/goals, fire extinguisher/emergencies) is a concrete system you can adapt directly to Indian bank accounts and SIPs, even though it's written for an Australian audience.
